name: Ballistic shoulder protectors
description: A pair of padded aramid shields for the shoulders and upper arms, each on a webbing tab that fixes under a vest's shoulder strap.
notes: Two coyote nylon pads laid side by side, each with a darker seam, two black press studs and a webbing tab with a hook and loop patch off its top. They fasten under a body armour vest's shoulder by hook and loop and snaps, which no standard names, so they keep the arms slot that earlier arm guards named until a shoulder standard exists (proposed in the report). CHECK VOLUME: the pads laid side by side with their tabs out make a larger box than the packed pair. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.

name: EOD jacket
description: A thick bomb disposal jacket of aramid, fire-resistant cloth and foam, with a high collar and a front pocket for a large hard plate.
notes: Folded olive drab bundle, quilted ridges along both sides, the high padded collar rolled along the back and the flapped plate pocket on top. The plate pocket is a grid sized to a front plate. The reference's tool subtype has no use in Deadvox. CHECK VOLUME (x2.2): the folded jacket stands stiff and full of padding, larger than the reference's packed volume. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.

name: Tactical EOD jacket
description: A lighter bomb disposal jacket of aramid, fire-resistant cloth and foam, cut to go over a plate carrier, with a pocket on each upper arm for a shoulder pad.
notes: Folded coyote bundle with a black front zip, a low padded collar along the back and the flapped deltoid pockets of both folded sleeves on top. Each deltoid pocket is a grid sized to one shoulder pad; the shoulder protectors are one item for the pair, so filling both pockets from it needs the pair split or a mount standard. The reference's tool subtype has no use in Deadvox. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.

name: Mild steel ESAPI plate
description: A front or back armour plate forged from mild steel, its edges bound in nylon and two straps buckled across it.
notes: Steel plate with a shooter's cut, bent round a 350 mm radius, olive drab edge binding and straps, black buckles. The medium and tempered plates share this model with their own steel finish. No slot: it is an insert that rides in a vest's plate pocket and cannot be worn alone, so it keeps encumbrance, wear and protection for when it is carried there. Armour from an insert in a pocket has no content rule yet; the report proposes a plate standard for it. CHECK VOLUME: the reference volume is the plate's material; the model's box includes the air under its curve. The worn look is pending: clothing gets inventory and ground models only until a fitted worn family exists.
